newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbekneftegaz sees major gas deal with Enron in '97.
newsitem.headline: Uzbekneftegaz sees major gas deal with Enron in '97.

text.p: Uzbekneftegaz, the state oil and gas firm of Uzbekistan, sees a planned $1.2 billion venture with Enron Oil & Gas Co of the United States getting off the ground this year, a top Uzbek company official said on Thursday.

"There is a definite plan to create a joint venture between Uzbekneftegaz and Enron -- I can be sure that it will be completed this year," said Ibrat Zaynutdinov, deputy general director of Uzbekneftegaz, at an energy conference.
"We have signed a lot of protocols with Enron in the past. We have solved all the technical questions and we are now negotiating the commercial details," he said. Enron officials declined to comment.

The joint project, to last at least 20 years, involves exploration and production of up to six billion cubic metres, or bcms, a year of natural gas in the former Soviet republic's Bukhara and Surkhan-Darya regions.
Zaynutdinov said that Gazprom could take part in the project but gave no details on how the Russian natural gas monopoly might participate.

The Central Asian state of Uzbekistan produced 50 bcms of natural gas in 1996, up slightly from 48.7 bcms in 1995. Uzbekistan's proven gas reserves at the end of 1995 were 1.9 trillion cubic metres, or 1.3 percent of total world reserves. RTR
